root_cause: High-frequency pg_cron jobs were aligned on the same minute boundaries while cron.use_background_workers=off, so each concurrent run consumed a database connection. Under load this caused pg_cron job startup timeouts, Supavisor session-pool checkout timeouts, and PostgREST schema-cache statement timeouts. Noncritical bg-interactie telemetry then amplified the incident by continuing to send a high volume of REST inserts during Data API degradation.
contributing_causes: The project has max_connections=60 while pg_cron allows up to 32 concurrent jobs.
Five */5 jobs, three */10 jobs, two */15 jobs, six hourly jobs at minute 17, and five daily jobs around 06:20 created deterministic fan-out peaks.
GitHub-hosted runners cannot rely on the project's direct IPv6 database endpoint; trusted migration repair must use the IPv4 Supavisor session pooler.
Three runtime-event writers used 'degraded' as lifecycle state even though the canonical powerhouse_runtime_events state contract allows only observed/decided/actioned/closed/ignored/error.
Nested analytical views re-evaluated the same buying-window/person/company intelligence chain multiple times, pushing research_queue and NBA v3+ beyond the database statement timeout.
prevention_rule: Spread database-backed cron schedules so recurring control-plane load stays bounded; keep GitHub database transport on the canonical IPv4 Supavisor session bridge; and make noncritical telemetry fail-open with a short Data API timeout and circuit breaker. Runtime degradation must map to lifecycle state 'error' while degradation detail remains in data_quality/evidence. Keep latency-critical read models single-pass: cache reusable freshness/contradiction state, split composite maintenance cron commands, and avoid rebuilding the same analytical view graph more than once per request.
